name: Cuts & Wounds
overview: Farm tools, wire, and equipment can cause cuts. Clean wounds promptly to prevent infection.

steps.title: Stop the bleeding
steps.detail: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth or gauze for 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Clean the wound
steps.detail: Rinse with clean running water. Remove dirt or debris. Soap around (not inside) the wound.

steps.title: Apply antibiotic ointment
steps.detail: Use if available. Cover with a clean bandage.

steps.title: Watch for infection
steps.detail: Watch for redness, swelling, pus, fever, or increasing pain. Change bandage daily.

steps.when_to_seek_help: Go to urgent care or ER if: bleeding won't stop after 15 minutes, wound is deep or gaping, cut is on face or over a joint, object is embedded, or you see signs of infection. Tetanus shot may be needed if it's been more than 5 years.
prevention_tips: Wear sturdy gloves when handling wire, tools, or machinery.
Keep tools sharp—dull blades slip and cause worse cuts.
